name: Finnish
script: Latin with extra letters: ä, ö (å in Swedish names only); left to right
basis: Suomen mestari 1 (Finn Lectura), chapters 1-9, as used in UCL's Finnish Level One
src: Finn Lectura: Suomen mestari 1 (renewed edition) sample pages PDF with the table of contents, chapters 1-9 with vocabulary and grammar
UCL SSEES: Finnish evening course Level One page, themes and grammar topics, textbook Suomen mestari 1
note: The order follows Suomen mestari 1 (pronouns, olla, vowel harmony; k-p-t gradation, verb type 1, negation, questions; genitive, t-plural; partitive, minulla on; verb types 1-5, verb + verb; location cases, tämä / tuo / se, imperative; word types, past of olla; mass-noun partitive, postpositions, directions). Splitting the sounds into two lessons, splitting the location cases into inner and outer, and all titles are my own judgment; colloquial spoken forms are left out. As in chapter 2 of the book, Puhutko suomea?, Mistä sinä olet? and prices are taught first as set phrases; the partitive and the location cases are explained in stage 3.
hardest: Long vs short sounds that change meaning: tuli / tuuli, kuka / kukka
Vowel harmony: every ending has two forms (-ssa / -ssä)
Consonant gradation: k-p-t change inside the word (nukkua, nukun)
Many cases, and when to use the partitive

items: Vowels and long sounds: ä, ö, y, and tuli vs tuuli
Double consonants and first-syllable stress: kuka vs kukka
Introducing yourself with olla: minä olen, sinä olet
Vowel harmony: front and back words
Consonant gradation k-p-t: nukkua, minä nukun
The negative verb: en, et, ei (en puhu)
Questions: mikä, kuka, missä, mistä, and -ko / -kö
Countries and languages: Mistä sinä olet?, Puhutko suomea?
Numbers and prices: Paljonko tämä maksaa?
Verb types 2-5: syödä, tulla, haluta, tarvita
Clock time and daily routine: Paljonko kello on?
Inner location cases: talossa, talosta, taloon
Outer location cases: torilla, torilta, torille
Huoneessa on…: there is, and tämä, tuo, se
Ordering food: Saisinko…?, and the partitive of mass nouns
Noun types -e, -nen, -i: huone, huoneessa; nainen, naisen
Past of olla and minulla oli: olin, olit, oli
Directions and postpositions: vasemmalle, oikealle, aseman vieressä
